lead.t: ○ Ankylosing spondylitis: Patients with UC have a 30 times greater incidence of ankylosing\nspondylitis than the general population; the course is independent of the colitis.

b: Destruction of articular cartilage + bony ankylosis, especially sacroiliac and vertebral apophyseal joints
Presents: lower back pain + spinal immobility; onset in 2nd–3rd decades
Peripheral joints (hips, knees, shoulders) involved in ≥1/3 of cases
Role of HLA-B27: presumably presents an antigen triggering the disease; specific antigen and pathogenic T cell remain unknown

Family history: Relatives with IBD, psoriasis, ankylosing spondylitis — Genetic predisposition (NOD2, IL23R) increases risk.
Inflammatory / rheumatic: Ankylosing spondylitis (vertebral fusion), rheumatoid pannus — Chronic inflammatory arthritis

The umbrella includes ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic arthritis, reactive arthritis, enteropathic arthritis and undifferentiated spondyloarthritis.
A patient on a TNF‑α inhibitor for ankylosing spondylitis develops a persistent cough and night sweats.

qs.q: Which of the following pathological features is uniquely shared by both rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis, but is entirely absent in osteoarthritis?
qs.e: Joint fusion (ankylosis, whether fibrous or bony) occurs in both rheumatoid arthritis and ankylosing spondylitis, whereas osteoarthritis explicitly lacks joint fusion. Osteophytes and bone eburnation are classic features of osteoarthritis.
